clue.text: Of modest dimensions when cut down to size

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to deflate someone's pride, used as a verb

explanation.walkthrough: One meaning is an adjective, the other a verb; the clue reads as a single description of shrinking something.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means lowly or small as an adjective, and as a verb it means to take someone's pride away and lower their standing.

clue.text: One's possibly spotted with French marshal back in Hawaii

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the creature, 'one is' plus a description

indicators.note: in places the marshal's name inside the letters standing for the island state

parts.note: HA is the old postal abbreviation for Hawaii

indicators.note: going back means the marshal's name is read from its end to its start

parts.note: Michel Ney was one of Napoleon's marshals

explanation.surface: A tourist in Hawaii might be spotted alongside a French military man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spotted' seems to mean seen, but it means having spots, as the spotted hyena does. Michel Ney was one of Napoleon's marshals.
explanation.definitionFit: The spotted hyena is the best-known species of this African scavenger, so the creature may well carry spots on its coat.

clue.text: Wrong to smear eminent conductor

indicators.note: something wrong is out of order, so the following letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A critic is told it is unfair to slander a celebrated orchestra leader.
explanation.definitionFit: A maestro is a distinguished musician, especially a renowned orchestral conductor, the title given to great masters of music.

clue.text: Nothing to compare with what Edward and Wallis made

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring
to match something is to equal or compare with it

explanation.surface: Nothing could equal the famous royal romance of Edward and Wallis.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward VIII gave up the British throne in 1936 to marry the American divorcee Wallis Simpson.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward and Wallis married purely for romance, at the cost of a crown, which is a marriage made for affection rather than advantage.

clue.text: Stiff found in church on street near the centre of Kilmarnock

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after, so church follows the rest

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street

indicators.note: the centre of keeps only the two middle letters of the Scottish town's name

parts.note: the two central letters of the ten-letter town name
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A stiff body discovered in a church on a street in the middle of Kilmarnock, a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stiff' suggests a corpse, but here it is the noun for the laundry stiffener used on collars. 'Found in' looks like a container signal but only links the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Starch is the substance used to stiffen collars and linen, so the noun names a stiffening agent; 'stiff' is slang for it.

clue.text: Care for Faith

definitions.meaning: first meaning: custody or charge, as in holding something in safekeeping
second meaning: confidence or belief in someone

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like an instruction to look after someone called Faith; the capital is a disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: Property held in trust is in someone's charge or keeping, and trusting a person means having confidence or belief in them.

clue.text: Signal to stop flushed German fellow climbing

parts.note: flushed in the face is red

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing reads the German fellow from bottom to top

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for German
Alf, a typical man's name, stands for any fellow

explanation.surface: A red-faced German man scaling something waves to bring things to a halt.
explanation.walkthrough: Alf is a stock crossword name for any man; climbing applies to German and fellow together.
explanation.definitionFit: A red flag is waved on racetracks, railways and beaches as a warning to halt or as a sign of danger.

clue.text: Extremely cooperative after animal managed to cause an obstruction

parts.note: a hind is a female deer
ran a business means managed it

indicators.note: taking a word at its extremes keeps just its first and last letters

parts.note: first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: An unusually helpful animal somehow ends up blocking the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' sends the two letters from cooperative to the end, though they come first in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A hindrance is something that gets in the way and impedes progress, which is exactly what any obstruction or blockage does.

clue.text: Hold back when about to help

parts.note: re means concerning or about
to serve someone is to help or assist them

explanation.surface: Someone hesitates at the moment they are about to lend a hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' looks like 'on the point of', but 'about' is RE and 'to help' is SERVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To reserve something is to keep it back or set it aside for later rather than using it now.

clue.text: Lacking interest in nude man cavorting

indicators.note: cavorting is leaping about wildly, so the letters jump into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A naked man prancing about turns out, surprisingly, to be rather boring.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mundane is ordinary and humdrum, dull and everyday, so it has nothing exciting about it.

clue.text: Depraved behaviour exhibited by queen getting tied up roughly after stud strips off

indicators.note: roughly means approximately or carelessly, so the letters are not in their exact order
stripping off the outside of a word leaves only its inner letters

parts.note: the word without its outer letters
R for Regina, Latin for queen
letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A queen bound up after a stud undresses suggests some fairly racy goings-on.
explanation.walkthrough: TU, then R, then the anagram of TIED UP: TU-R-PITUDE. The surface's bondage picture fits the definition neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: Turpitude means wickedness or moral corruption, used mainly in the phrase moral turpitude for vile, depraved conduct.

clue.text: The same as having to flog endless rubbish to get on

indicators.note: with no end, the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them
tat is cheap junk
to mount a horse is to get on it

explanation.surface: Selling junk to make a living is little better than a con.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flog' is British slang for sell, the false path; here it means beat, giving TAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Tantamount, usually followed by 'to', means equivalent in effect or significance, so something tantamount is effectively identical.

clue.text: Unerring Latin for 'small decoy'

indicators.note: putting one thing for another means swapping it in to replace the other

parts.note: an unerring shot is a sure one
L is the abbreviation for Latin
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A translation note, giving the precise Latin term for a little decoy.
explanation.walkthrough: In SURE, the S is replaced by L. 'Small decoy' looks like one phrase, but 'small' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A lure is bait or an enticement used to draw prey or people into a trap, just as a decoy does.

clue.text: Shoot right away — Go on!

indicators.note: sending a letter away removes it from the word

parts.note: a shoot of a plant is a sprout
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: An impatient cry urging someone to fire immediately and get on with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoot' and 'Go on!' both look like urgings to speak, but 'Shoot' is the plant sprout.
explanation.definitionFit: To spout is to talk at length, pompously or without stopping, which is what 'go on' means when someone rambles.

clue.text: Maiden stopping conscious of general opinion

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap, so the letter sits inside the other word

parts.note: sentient means aware or conscious
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A young woman interrupting a general who is aware of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of general opinion' looks like one phrase, but 'of' is the link. M goes inside SENTIENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentiment can mean a view or attitude held widely, as in public sentiment, a prevailing feeling among people.

clue.text: Ringing to find information kept in factory

indicators.note: something kept in a building sits inside it, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: a plant is an industrial works
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Phoning around to discover details held at a manufacturing works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ringing' looks like telephoning; it is the adjective for a resonant sound, like a bell.
explanation.definitionFit: Plangent describes a loud, resonant, often mournful sound, like a bell or a plucked string reverberating.

clue.text: Verify sectarian slaughter

indicators.note: slaughter hacks a thing to pieces, so the letters are scattered and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A request to confirm reports of religious killings.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascertain is to find out for certain or make sure of something, which is to check and confirm it.

clue.text: Photo showing ball after game

parts.note: snap is a card game
shot is the metal ball fired from a cannon or put in athletics

explanation.surface: A picture of a ball taken once the match is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' reverses the clue's order, so the game comes first in the answer and the ball second.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapshot is an informal photograph taken quickly, usually with a handheld camera and no posing.

clue.text: Part of Poins penned by playwright after a drop of porter

indicators.note: a single drop is just the first bit of the drink

parts.note: first letter of the word

indicators.note: something penned by a writer is enclosed within them, as in a pen

parts.note: Joe Orton was an English playwright
Poins is this puzzle's setter, who refers to themselves as I

explanation.surface: The setter wonders about a role written by a dramatist, perhaps Poins in Shakespeare, after a sip of dark beer.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often name themselves for I. P then ORTON with I inside. Porter is a dark beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A portion is a share or section of a larger whole, so it is simply one part of something.

clue.text: A couple of acolytes discovered in revolutionary's hiding place

indicators.note: something discovered in a place is found inside it

parts.note: Che Guevara, the Marxist revolutionary

indicators.note: a couple means two, so just the first pair of letters is taken

parts.note: first two letters of the word

explanation.surface: Two church servers are found in a rebel's secret hideout.
explanation.walkthrough: The revolutionary is Che Guevara; the possessive simply joins him to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cache is a hidden store of goods or weapons, or the secret place where such things are concealed.

clue.text: Set books leading to anger rising in church

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces within the abbreviation for church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

indicators.note: in a down entry rising reads the word for anger from bottom to top

parts.note: ire is wrath

explanation.surface: Religious texts provoke growing fury in a congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' looks like a verb, but it is the noun for a social circle.
explanation.definitionFit: A coterie is a small exclusive circle of people with shared interests, which is one sense of a set or clique.

clue.text: Level of River Bann's first to drop

indicators.note: to drop a letter is to let it fall out of the word

parts.note: the Tiber is the river through Rome

indicators.note: the first of the Northern Irish river's name is just its opening letter

parts.note: first letter of the name

explanation.surface: A question about the water level of the River Bann, a river in Northern Ireland, as it falls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'River Bann' reads as one name, but River is TIBER and only the B of Bann is used, then removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is one of a series of rows or layers placed one above another, so it is a level or stage.

clue.text: Get subordinate to adopt a resolute attitude

parts.note: under means lower in rank
taking a stand means holding a firm position

explanation.surface: Persuade a junior employee to take a firm line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get' looks like 'persuade', but it is the definition, in the sense 'I get it'.
explanation.definitionFit: To get something can mean to grasp or comprehend it, as in 'I get the joke'.

clue.text: American puma regularly seen near the middle of Wimbledon Common

parts.note: US for American

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the big cat is kept

parts.note: second and fourth letters

indicators.note: the middle of keeps only the central letter of the London district

parts.note: fifth of nine letters

explanation.surface: A big cat from America is regularly spotted on Wimbledon Common, a park in south-west London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wimbledon Common' reads as one place, but 'Common' is the definition. Big-cat sightings in British parks are a newspaper staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Usual and common both describe what happens often or is ordinary and customary, so they are close synonyms.

clue.text: Section of organic herbs aimed at a specialised market

indicators.note: a section of the phrase is a run of letters cut from inside it

parts.note: a run of consecutive letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A shop department of organic herbs targets a narrow group of buyers.
explanation.walkthrough: Hidden in orgaNIC HErbs. The definition is the adjective, as in niche marketing.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, the word describes products or services that target a small specialised group of customers.

clue.text: Bitterly regret carrying money on European train

indicators.note: carrying means holding something within, so the other pieces go inside

parts.note: to rue is to regret bitterly

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after, so the money follows the European

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European
tin is old slang for money

explanation.surface: A passenger deeply regrets taking cash onto a train across Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' looks like a railway train, but it is the followers trailing a dignitary. Tin is old slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: A retinue is the group of attendants following an important person, also called that person's train.

clue.text: Jeer when Obama embraces Republican

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so one word wraps around the letter

parts.note: Barack Obama, the US president
R for Republican

explanation.surface: Heckling breaks out when the Democratic president hugs a political opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: To barrack is British for heckling a speaker or player. R goes inside the forename BARACK.
explanation.definitionFit: To barrack is to jeer at or shout down a speaker or player, a common British and Australian verb.

clue.text: Go and consider leaving Henry out against the French

indicators.note: leaving a letter out drops it from the word

parts.note: to think something over is to consider it
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Advice to leave and reconsider, without Henry, against the French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' looks like an instruction to depart, but it is the euphemism for urinating. 'Against' just places LE beside TINK.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinkle is a coy, childish word for urinating, and 'go' is a common euphemism for the same act.

clue.text: Exist essentially in loveless heroine surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly means unexpectedly, so the letters turn up in an unexpected order
without love means losing the zero-shaped letter that love stands for

parts.note: taken as written
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A literary heroine who unexpectedly finds herself without love.
explanation.walkthrough: HEROINE without O leaves HERINE, which is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To inhere is to be an intrinsic, permanent part of something, existing in it as an essential quality.
